'''Robert Mackenzie Johnston''' [[Fellow of the Linnean Society|F.L.S.]], (27 November 1843 – 20 April 1918)<ref name=ADB>R. L. Wettenhall, '[https://adb.anu.edu.au/biography/johnston-robert-mackenzie-6863 Johnston, Robert Mackenzie (1843 - 1918)]', ''[[Australian Dictionary of Biography]]'', Volume 9, [[Melbourne University Press|MUP]], 1983, pp 501-503. Retrieved 8 November 2012</ref> was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]]-[[Australians|Australian]] [[statistician]] and [[scientist]].

==Early life==
Johnston was born at Petty<ref name=Mennell>{{cite Australasia|Johnston, Robert Mackenzie}}</ref> near [[Inverness]], [[Scotland]], the son of Lachlan Johnstone,<ref name=Mennell/> a [[crofter]], and his wife Mary, ''née'' Mackenzie.<ref name=ADB/> Johnston studied [[botany]], [[geology]], and [[chemistry]] at the [[Andersonian University]] under Professors Kennedy, Crosskey, and Penny.<ref name=Mennell/>

==Career in Australia==
In the 1870s he wrote  "Field Memoranda for Tasmanian Botanists" (Launceston, 1874). In 1880 he became chief clerk in the Audit Department, his former railway colleagues presented him with a watch inscribed: {{cquote|Presented to ROBERT MACKENZIE JOHNSTON by personal friends, on the occasion of his going from amongst them, in recognition not merely of his scientific attainments, but also of his social worth, and as a token of the high esteem and great regard in which he has been ever hold. Launceston, Tasmania, August, 1880. ''Invitum sequitur honos''.}}<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article38262188 |title=PRESENTATION TO R. M. JOHNSTON ESQ. |publisher=Trove, National Library of Australia |date=3 September 1880 |work=Launceston Examiner |accessdate=8 November 2012}}</ref>

He also was the author of "Descriptive Catalogue of Tasmanian Fishes" (Hobart, 1882).  

==Legacy==
Johnston died at [[Hobart]] on 20 April 1918 of heart disease.<ref name=ADB/> Johnston received the Imperial Service Order in 1903 and was fellow of the [[Linnean Society of London]] and the Royal Geographical Society of Australasia and honorary fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] of London.

Species named in honor of Robert Mackenzie Johnston include the fish: Johnston's weedfish, ''[[Heteroclinus johnstoni]]'', and the Tasmanian yellow gum ''[[Eucalyptus johnstonii]]''.
